summary: One wrong-socket bug was reproduced and fixed. A later independent Opus 5.5 review confirmed an additional P2 RPC defect and model/test gaps. The original 134-state result has a close-guard mutation blind spot and is not a whole-program proof.

modeled: One FrameConnection, two frame operations, close/abort and descriptor-number reuse.
Frame acquisition and close use separate locked actions; each syscall is a separate transfer action.
abstracted: Payload/framing contents, descriptor integers, time and kernel scheduling.
Private duplicate lifetime is represented by a lease; successful duplication is assumed, because failure rejects the operation safely.
Each syscall returns in one step; blocked-I/O liveness is not proved.
A real EOF/error can return earlier; permitting both finite transfer steps overapproximates I/O for safety and does not verify error handling.
out_of_scope: Guest vsock flow control, VM destruction, process crashes, and hostile external close of an owned descriptor.
Unbounded theorem proving, OS implementation correctness and production failure frequency.
assumptions: NSLock serializes duplicate acquisition and close.
F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC retains the same open file description while the original integer may be reused.
Only the frame's defer releases its private duplicate.
The code/model correspondence was reviewed manually, not proved as Swift refinement.

properties.name: NoForeignIO
properties.meaning: A frame never reads from or writes to an unrelated socket after descriptor reuse.
properties.bounds: 1 connection, 2 frame operations, 2 syscalls per operation, 1 descriptor reuse; all reachable states; no fairness/state constraints

properties.name: NoLateAcquire
properties.meaning: A new frame operation cannot acquire a live descriptor after close.

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in [Ops -> {"idle", "pending", "active", "done"}]
    /\ calls \in [Ops -> 0..2]
    /\ slot \in {"original", "free", "foreign"}
    /\ closed \in BOOLEAN /\ foreignIO \in BOOLEAN /\ lateAcquire \in BOOLEAN
properties.meaning: Every generated state has fully assigned variables within the finite domains.

findings.title: Framed socket I/O can cross into a different connection after close
findings.story: FrameConnection serialized writes and made close idempotent, but its read/write loops still used the released descriptor integer. A subsequent socket can reuse that number. A stale writer then transmits old payload to the new socket, and a stale reader consumes the new socket's bytes. AgentClient replacement and concurrent exec stdin/output make delayed operations relevant production callers; the reproduction establishes the code path, not its field frequency.

trace.action: Submit then Acquire; baseline uses the original descriptor number without an owned lease
Close releases the original descriptor number
Reuse the same number for a different socket
Transfer uses the stale integer and accesses the unrelated socket

reproduction.detail: The two deterministic dup2 tests replay Close -> Reuse -> stale I/O: they fail on property assertions against unchanged Agent.swift and pass after the fix. The third test observes header consumption before close; before the fix its read did not finish by the deadline, so it is not claimed as a demonstrated mixed-frame transfer. After the fix it returns promptly and preserves the unrelated socket's body.

fix.summary: Check closed and duplicate the socket under closeLock; hold a private CLOEXEC descriptor through the entire read or write frame, releasing it with defer. Close also shuts the socket down, waking operations on duplicates. Public signatures and wire framing are unchanged.

diagram.title: Before the fix, closing a connection lets its old I/O address an unrelated socket.

sanity_checks: Mutation: NoForeignIO fails again (77 generated, 50 distinct states, depth 6).
NeverCompletes intentionally fails (135 generated, 76 distinct states, depth 7).
NeverReuses intentionally fails (13 generated, 10 distinct states, depth 3).
All six protocol/environment actions have positive coverage; terminal stuttering is evaluated four times.
Frozen Properties.tla sha256 is unchanged from before the bug check.

Independent review: removing the Acquire closed guard while LeaseFD=TRUE still passes (254 generated / 108 distinct states, depth 13). The original fix-toggle check did not sufficiently validate regression sensitivity. See docs/review-2026-10-29-opus55.md.

notes: TLC uses finite-state enumeration with fingerprints; no Lean/unbounded proof or axioms audit is claimed.
An initial model draft had an incompletely specified disjunction; parentheses were corrected before producing the cited counterexample. Frozen protocol properties were not changed.
Full evidence logs are retained. Absolute paths/pids in local test logs identify the test environment, not a deployment.

The follow-up review and parent reproductions are saved under evidence/opus55. The original model/Properties.tla and historical logs are unchanged; the passing original invariants must be interpreted with the newly documented mutation blind spot.

review.summary: Follow-up is required: a second frame-lease EMFILE can leave RPC responses misaligned; the original model misses removal of the close guard; all three socket tests still pass without close shutdown. The parent also confirmed a test-only descriptor-table isolation defect. No product fix or new release is part of this review.
